name: FurnitureBench
ability_definition: The ability to quickly move your hand, your hand together with your arm, or your two hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects.

task_realism.reasoning: The tasks are real physical assembly of furniture-like objects. They require grasping, re-orienting, inserting and screwing, which are the core elements of manual assembly work. The furniture is simplified, 3D-printed and tag-instrumented rather than production parts, and the tasks are fixed and repetitive. Still, the manipulation demands closely resemble bench assembly jobs.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation runs on real hardware under a standardized lab setup: fixed camera placement, AprilTag pose markers, a controlled background and set randomness levels. Real workplaces have variable lighting, clutter, part tolerances, interruptions and throughput pressure. Episode horizon limits exist, but speed is not scored. Many reported results use state input from the benchmark's own markers or come from simulation, which weakens the match to real conditions. Small trial counts, such as 20 real-world trials, add noise.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers the grasp–manipulate–assemble portion of the definition well, including long-horizon multi-step assembly. It misses two explicit parts of the definition. First, 'quickly' is not measured, since there is no timing metric. Second, 'two hands together' is absent, since it uses a single arm with a parallel-jaw gripper and has no bimanual tasks. Fine finger-level dexterity and in-hand manipulation are also largely excluded.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are physical objects and camera or proprioceptive observations. The output is a physically assembled object, judged on completion. This is a natural, non-artificial format close to real assembly outcomes. Points are deducted for the fiducial-marked, simplified parts and for binary or phase-based success scoring rather than workplace quality criteria.

transferability_reasoning: FurnitureBench is among the more realistic manipulation benchmarks, because it requires genuine multi-step physical assembly with grasping, reorientation, insertion and screwing on real hardware. Its transfer to the full Manual Dexterity construct is limited by three gaps: it does not score speed, it has no bimanual tasks, it uses a single parallel gripper, and its lab conditions are controlled and marker-assisted. It is a solid but partial proxy for real workplace dexterity.

2024.model_or_system: DPPO (Diffusion Policy Policy Optimization), trained in simulation and transferred zero-shot to a real Franka robot
2024.metric: task success rate (%) on real-world FurnitureBench One-leg assembly, 20 hardware trials
2024.human_reference: General adult workforce performing manual assembly (e.g., assembly or warehouse workers, typical adults assembling flat-pack furniture)
